reviews.text: Terrible service, and they overcharge for their services. They returned my cat covered in urine; that's inhumane. And they claim to be such a great veterinary center. Even the one on the corner doesn't treat them like that. Please don't go there. Look for another option.

On Monday, June 12th, Dr. Rafael Ramírez discharged Pechitos following his femur surgery performed on June 15th. I would like to express my deepest gratitude to the orthopedic staff for their kind, empathetic, and wonderful care of Pechitos throughout his stay. They were always highly professional in their work. I also want to thank the staff in the X-ray department, pharmacy, reception, and so on. Many thanks to everyone.

In particular, I want to sincerely thank Drs. Aldo Ortega, Luis Arellano, Cesar Sanchez, and Rafael Ramirez for the excellent surgeries they performed on Pechitos, their recommendations, their always caring treatment of Pechitos, and their evident professionalism.
It's a hospital with highly qualified doctors; they explained the entire procedure for my dog ​​very well, and I recommend it 100%.

They treated us on a Sunday for an unexplained hemorrhage, they took exceptional care of our dog, the costs aren't cheap but they aren't expensive either (much less for a Sunday) and most importantly, they had the opportunity to operate on our dog and avoided it at all costs, this strikes me as a place with ethics...

Perhaps five years ago or more they were good, but now, between the rude and apathetic service from the receptionist and the lack of timely tests, I'm disappointed. I took my dog ​​there two days ago because she started having bloody diarrhea and vomiting. Besides, the cost is $1000 just for an examination (not even for a human; today, for example, I went to Hospital de la Luz for an eye emergency and they charge $700, while the private clinic charges $1000). I didn't feel confident with the doctor. He was very friendly, but basically, he wanted me to decide whether to take her to internal medicine or if he would just give her medication and, depending on the results, if she got worse, I would take her back to the emergency room, and if not, then to internal medicine. I decided to take her to the emergency room and pay precisely to PREVENT her from getting worse. I didn't want to pay to see if she would get worse or not. They're supposed to know that the medication they're going to give her is meant to make her better, and the doctor was like... what do you prefer? Should I go to internal medicine or give her the medication myself? I don't know if maybe she's still a trainee, or why, since I was already in a consultation that they were clearly going to charge me for, why not just give me the medication that was supposed to cure her?
Now she's had bloody diarrhea for two days and I'm worried sick. To make matters worse, I asked for an ultrasound to check for any perforations or to get a proper look and not just guess the cause of the bloody diarrhea, since I explained that she ate grass and defecated it as is. And it turns out that on Thursday at 6 pm, the doctor who does ultrasounds had left at 4 pm and there was no one available to do them. So HOW IS IT THAT A VETERINARY EMERGENCY HOSPITAL DOESN'T HAVE THE TECHNICAL EQUIPMENT TO DO ULTRASOUNDS?

I went to this clinic on the recommendation of my veterinarian to have my dog's ultrasound done. My experience with the service was unsatisfactory for several reasons.

The first time, the receptionist told me that a doctor's order wasn't necessary. However, when I arrived for the appointment, they informed me that they couldn't perform the ultrasound without it and turned me away. This caused me to waste time and miss work unnecessarily, a situation I believe could have been avoided if they had provided me with accurate information about the requirements from the initial contact.

The second time, they brought my dog ​​in alone for the ultrasound. I understand that each clinic has its own protocols, and I respect how they operate, although in other clinics I've visited, the owner is allowed to accompany their pet during the procedure.

Furthermore, they told me the results would be available within three business days, but the report took a week to arrive, and I had to insist to get it sent. I believe that if a delivery time is established, it should be respected, or failing that, any delays should be communicated promptly.

Fortunately, in my dog's case, the test wasn't urgent. However, I feel that the communication, organization, and efficiency of the service left much to be desired. My dissatisfaction isn't limited to the waiting times, but also includes the lack of accurate information and the follow-up I had to undertake to receive a service I paid for.

I hope you can take these comments as an opportunity for improvement, since proper service involves not only performing the tests correctly, but also providing clear information, respecting established timelines, and offering a satisfactory experience for both patients and their owners.
